questions.topic: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Compound (X), shown below, dissolves in $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution and has two chiral carbon atoms
Statement II: Compound (Y), shown below, has two carbons with $sp^{3}$ hybridization, one carbon with $sp^{2}$ and one carbon with $sp$ hybridization
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
[Structure of X with the two chiral carbons marked *]
Soluble in $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$, because of COOH group
[Structure of Y: the two chain carbons are $sp^{3}$; in $\mathrm{C{=}C{=}O}$ the first carbon is $sp^{2}$ and the second is $sp$]

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.stem: The correct increasing order of $\mathrm{C-H}\,(A)$, $\mathrm{C-O}\,(B)$, $\mathrm{C=O}\,(C)$ and $\mathrm{C \equiv N}\,(D)$ bonds in terms of covalent bond length is :

In a closed 1 L vessel, 1 bar A(g) is allowed to decompose at T(K). After 100 minutes, the total pressure was 1.5 bar. What is the rate constant (in $\mathrm{min^{-1}}$) of the reaction ? ($\log 2 = 0.3$)

Given below are four compounds :
(a) n-propyl choride
(b) iso-propyl chloride
(c) sec-butyl chloride
(d) neo-pentyl chloride
Percentage of carbon in the one which exhibits optical isomerism is :
questions.solution:
Here sec-butyl chloride is optically active

$$\text{percentage of carbon} = \frac{48}{92.5} \times 100 = 51.9\%$$

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.stem:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I (Pair of Compounds) | List - II (Type of Isomers)
A. 2-Methylpropene and but-1-ene | I. Stereoisomers
B. Cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene | II. Position isomers
C. 2-Butanol and diethyl ether | III. Chain isomers
D. But-1-ene and but-2-ene | IV. Functional group isomers
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
(A) 2-methylpropene & but-1-ene $\rightarrow$ chain isomer
(B) cis-but-2-ene & trans-but-2-ene $\rightarrow$ stereo isomer
(C) 2-butanol & diethyl ether $\rightarrow$ functional group
(D) but-1-ene & but-2-ene $\rightarrow$ position isomer

questions.stem:
Consider the following data:
$\Delta_f H^{\ominus}$ (methane, g) $= -X\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Enthalpy of sublimation of graphite $= Y\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{H_2} = Z\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
The bond enthalpy of $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond is given by :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C(graphite) + 2H_2(g) \xrightarrow{-x} CH_4(g)}$
$\mathrm{C(graphite)} \xrightarrow{+Y} \mathrm{C(gas)}$ ; $\mathrm{2H_2(g)} \xrightarrow{+2Z} \mathrm{4H(g)}$ ; $\mathrm{C(gas) + 4H(g)} \xrightarrow{-4W} \mathrm{CH_4(g)}$
$$Y + 2Z - 4W = -x$$
$$W = \frac{x + y + 2z}{4}$$

questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) of $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$ is greater than that of $\mathrm{[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$.
Statement II: Potassium ferricyanide has a greater spin-only magnetic moment than sodium ferrocyanide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement I :
$\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}\ (3d^{4})$ : CFSE $= -0.6\,\Delta_0$
$\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\ (3d^{5})$ : CFSE $= 0$ (because of $d^{5}$)
Statement II :
Patassium ferricyanide $\rightarrow \mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\ (\mu = \sqrt{3})$
Sodium ferrocyanide $\rightarrow \mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\ (\mu = 0)$

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.stem:
Aqueous HCl reacts with $\mathrm{MnO_2(s)}$ to form $\mathrm{MnCl_2(aq)}$, $\mathrm{Cl_2(g)}$ $\mathrm{H_2O}(l)$. What is the weight (in g) of $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ liberated when 8.7 g of $\mathrm{MnO_2(s)}$ is reacted with excess aqueous HCl solution ?
(Given Molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ Mn = 55, Cl = 35.5, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{MnO_2 + 4HCl \rightarrow MnCl_2 + Cl_2 + 2H_2O}$
$$n_{\mathrm{MnO_2}} = n_{\mathrm{Cl_2}} = \frac{8.7}{87} = 0.1$$
mass of $\mathrm{Cl_2} = 0.1 \times 71 = 7.1$

questions.stem:

B. $\mathrm{SnCl_2, HCl}$ | II. Rosenmund Reduction

questions.stem:
Consider the following spectral lines for atomic hydrogen :
A. First line of Paschen series
B. Second line of Balmer series
C. Third line of Paschen series
D. Fourth line of Bracket series
The correct arrangement of the above lines in ascending order of energy is :
questions.solution:
$$\Delta E \propto \left(\frac{1}{n_1^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_2^{2}}\right) \text{value}$$
(A) $\rightarrow n_1 = 3$, $n_2 = 4$
(B) $\rightarrow n_1 = 2$, $n_2 = 4$
(C) $\rightarrow n_1 = 3$, $n_2 = 6$
(D) $\rightarrow n_1 = 4$, $n_2 = 8$

questions.stem:
By usual analysis, 1.00 g of compound (X) gave 1.79 g of magnesium pyrophosphate. The percentage of phosphorus in compound (X) is : (nearest integer)
(Given, molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ : O = 16, Mg = 24, P = 31)

Given below are some of the statements about Mn and $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$. Identify the correct statements.
A. Mn forms the oxide $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$, in which Mn is in its highest oxidation state.
B. Oxygen stabilizes the Mn in higher oxidation states by forming multiple bonds with Mn .
C. $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$ is an ionic oxide.
D. The structure of $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$ consists of one bridged oxygen.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
(A) Highest O.N of Mn is $+7$
(B) Mn generally form stable comp. in highest O.N with oxygen.
(C) $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$ is covalent because of Higher O.N.
(D) $\mathrm{O_3Mn-O-MnO_3}$ (one bridging O; each Mn has three Mn=O bonds)

questions.stem:
A substance 'X' (1.5 g) dissolved in 150 g of a solvent 'Y' (molar mass = 300 $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) led to an elevation of the boiling point by 0.5 K . The relative lowering in the vapour pressure of the solvent 'Y' is ________ $\times 10^{-2}$. (nearest integer)
[Given : $K_b$ of the solvent = 5.0 $\mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$]
Assume the solution to be dilute and no association or dissociation of X takes place in solution.
questions.solution:
$\Delta T_b = i\,k_b\,m$
$0.5 = i \times m \times 5$
$m = 0.1$
$$\frac{P_O - P_s}{P_O} = \frac{m \times M_{\mathrm{solvent}}}{1000} = \frac{0.1 \times 300}{1000} = 0.03$$

questions.stem:
MX is a sparingly soluble salt that follows the given solubility equilibrium at 298 K .
$\mathrm{MX(s) \rightleftharpoons M^+(aq) + X^-(aq)}$; $K_{sp} = 10^{-10}$
If the standard reduction potential for $\mathrm{M^+(aq) \xrightarrow{+e^-} M(s)}$ is $\left(E^{\ominus}_{\mathrm{M^+/M}}\right) = 0.79\ \mathrm{V}$, then the value of the standard reduction potential for the metal/metal insoluble salt electrode $E^{\ominus}_{\mathrm{X^-/MX(s)/M}}$ is ________ mV. (nearest integer)
[Given : $\dfrac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\ \mathrm{V}$]
questions.solution:
$$E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cl^-|AgCl|Ag}} = E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Ag^+|Ag}} - \frac{.059}{1}\log\frac{1}{k_{sp}}$$
$= 0.79 - .059 \log 10^{10}$
$= 0.2$ volt
$= 200$ mV

questions.stem:
The osmotic pressure of a living cell is 12 atm at 300 K . The strength of sodium chloride solution that is isotonic with the living cell at this temperature is ______ $\mathrm{g\,L^{-1}}$. (Nearest integer)
Given : R = 0.08 $\mathrm{L\,atm\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$
Assume complete dissociation of NaCl
(Given : Molar mass of Na and Cl are 23 and 35.5 $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ respectively.)
questions.solution:
$\pi = iMRT$
$12 = 2 \times M \times .08 \times 300$
$$M = \frac{1}{4}\,\frac{\text{mole}}{\text{lit}}$$
$$M = \frac{1}{4} \times 58.5\,\frac{\text{gm}}{\text{lit}}$$
$$M = 14.62\,\frac{\text{gm}}{\text{lit}}$$

questions.stem: The first and second ionization constants of $\mathrm{H_2X}$ are $2.5 \times 10^{-8}$ and $1.0 \times 10^{-13}$ respectively. The concentration of $\mathrm{X^{2-}}$ in 0.1 M $\mathrm{H_2X}$ solution is ______ $\times 10^{-15}$ M. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{H_2X \rightleftharpoons H^+ + HX^-}$
$0.1 - x$ ; $x + y$ ; $x - y$
$\mathrm{HX^- \rightleftharpoons H^+ + X^{2-}}$
$x - y$ ; $x + y$ ; $y$
$$\frac{(x+y)(x+y)}{0.1 - x} = 2.5 \times 10^{-8}$$
$$\frac{(x+y)(y)}{(x-y)} = 10^{-3}$$
$x >>> y$
$$[\mathrm{X^{2-}}] = y = 10^{-13}$$

questions.stem: Identify the metal ions among $\mathrm{Co^{2+}, Ni^{2+}, Fe^{2+}, V^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$ having a spin-only magnetic moment value more than 3.0 BM . The sum of unpaired electrons present in the high spin octahedral complexes formed by those metal ions is ______ .
questions.solution:
Only $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ can form high spin octahedral complex
$\mathrm{Fe^{2+}} \rightarrow 3d^{6} \rightarrow t_{2g}^{4} e_g^{2}$ : $n = 4$, $\mu > 3$
$\mathrm{Co^{2+}} \rightarrow 3d^{7} \rightarrow t_{2g}^{5} e_g^{2}$ : $n = 3$, $\mu > 3$
$= 3 + 4 = 7$
